/chrome-validate — column-alignment self-test

Two tables, same data. The first uses default flex per row (children sized to content) — this is the original bug pattern from PR #22, where each row sizes its columns to its own content and the columns drift out of alignment with the header. The second uses a shared CSS-grid template on every row, so column N has one deterministic width across the whole table.

The column-alignment sub-check should produce allOK: false for #bad > div and allOK: true for #good > div.

#bad — independent flex rows, children sized to content (expected: FAIL)

Verify in the browser console

function check(sel) {
  const rows = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(sel));
  const header = rows[0];
  const dataRows = rows.slice(1);
  const tol = 2;
  const out = [];
  let allOK = true;
  for (let col = 0; col < header.children.length; col++) {
    const h = header.children[col].getBoundingClientRect();
    const rs = dataRows.map(r => r.children[col].getBoundingClientRect());
    const maxAbs = Math.max(...rs.flatMap(r => [Math.abs(r.left - h.left), Math.abs(r.right - h.right)]));
    const ok = maxAbs <= tol;
    if (!ok) allOK = false;
    out.push({ col, name: header.children[col].textContent.trim(), maxAbsΔ: +maxAbs.toFixed(2), OK: ok });
  }
  return { allOK, columns: out };
}
check('#bad > div');   // expected: allOK === false
check('#good > div');  // expected: allOK === true
